newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Metlife urges S.Africa economic plan action.
newsitem.headline: Metlife urges S.Africa economic plan action.

text.p: Insurance group Metropolitan Life Ltd said on Thursday the government needed to take concrete action on its macro-economic strategy to revive business confidence.

"Both foreign and local investors need to see some visible signs of the successful implementation by government of its macro-economic strategy and crime prevention programme if their confidence is to be restored," Metlife Chairman Nthato Motlana said in his annual report.
"The gradual lifting of exchange controls will also boost confidence."
Motlana said strides made recently in black economic empowerment had introduced "a vibrancy and dynamism" to the public sector.

Metlife, a member of the National Empowerment Consortium (NEC) which last year won control of conglomerate Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic), has invested 264.6 million rand in Johnnic for a 3.4 percent stake, Motlana said.
"We have also provided funding of 470.3 million rand to other members of the NEC against security of their Johnnic shares and on terms which are linked to the performance of Johnnic shares," he said.
"We hope that the close relationship which will emerge between ourselves and all other members of the NEC will present us both with worthwhile business opportunities."

He said Metlife could expect a boost in single premium business from the large-scale retrenchments taking place in the public sector, but the lack of disposable income would limit growth in the life assurance market.

"Much will depend on government's approach to the recommendations of the Katz Commission (on tax) and on whether there will be any change to the 17 percent tax on the interest and net rental income of retirement funds which was introduced as an interim measure in this year's budget," Motlana said.
"The impact of the tax was difficult to determine, but it is possible that a shift took place from individual retirement annuities to normal individual endowment insurance."
Motlana said the central Reserve Bank had given Metlife the go-ahead to invest 20 million rand in a new life company, Metlife Botswana.
